15:Tc9ef,<p>I wanted to know whether these things nest, one inside another like a matryoshka doll, so I tried it. Claude Code lets you configure four: skills, agents, tools, hooks. Pair them up and you get sixteen combinations. I ran all sixteen.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>allowed-tools</code> lists Read and nothing else, the skill body triggers Bash, and Bash runs anyway even though it is not on the list</li>
<li>Once you invoke a skill carrying <code>hooks:</code>, that hook stays for the rest of the session. It does not go away when the skill finishes</li>
<li>One extra <code>e</code> in a hook's event name in <code>settings.json</code>, <code>PreToolUsee</code>: no error, no trigger. Add <code>--debug</code> or <code>--include-hook-events</code> to check and there is still no error message, only the hook events that should have been there are missing</li>
</ul>
<p>Environment:</p>
<ul>
<li>CLI 2.1.257, invoked as <code>~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.257</code> every time, never through the <code>claude</code> symlink, which updates itself</li>
<li>Agent SDK pinned at 0.3.257</li>
<li>every run under <code>-p</code> (<code>--print</code>): one prompt in, the result printed, then exit, with no interactive session and no dialogs</li>
</ul>
<h2>model and engine</h2>
<p>The <code>model</code> is Opus, Fable and the rest: the language model reached over the API. When it wants to call a tool, its reply carries an extra <code>tool_use</code> block:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"tool_use"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"name"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Bash"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"input"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: {</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"git status"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>That JSON is text the model wrote. <code>git status</code> has not run at this point.</p>
<p>The <code>engine</code> is the <code>claude</code> binary running locally. It hands the tool list to the model, runs whatever <code>tool_use</code> comes back, and on either side of that run checks <code>settings.json</code> for hooks.</p>
<p>Every separate context the engine spins up to get something done is a subagent. The main line counts as one too. Each context has its own tool list: one for the main line, one for each subagent.</p>
<p>Of the four primitives below, skills and agents are <code>.md</code> files on disk, hooks live in <code>settings.json</code> or frontmatter, and tools have no file at all. They do nothing on their own; the behaviour comes from the model and the engine reading them.</p>
<h2>The four</h2>
<h3>tool</h3>
<p>A tool is a function the model can call. A name and a parameter schema, nothing else.</p>
<p>The list has <code>Bash</code> on it and no <code>git status</code>. Ask the model to run <code>git status</code> and what it issues is one <code>Bash</code> call, with <code>git status</code> as the argument. To be a tool, a thing has to be registered in this session's tool list; unregistered, the model cannot see it and cannot call it.</p>
<p>A tool on that list is not itself a process. <code>Bash</code> is a name plus an argument shape, and the command only reaches a shell once the tool is called.</p>
<p>Built-in tool names are single words: <code>Read</code>, <code>Write</code>, <code>Edit</code>, <code>Bash</code>.</p>
<p>MCP servers hand you this format:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>mcp__&#x3C;server>__&#x3C;tool></code></li>
<li><code>mcp__claude_ai_Jira__getJiraIssue</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Capitalised, <code>Agent</code> and <code>Skill</code> are tools as well, sitting on the same list as <code>Bash</code> and <code>Read</code>; lowercase, agent and skill are <code>.md</code> files on disk, saying who the agent plays or what steps the skill follows. Starting a subagent is the model calling <code>Agent</code>; running a skill is the model calling <code>Skill</code>. A <code>SKILL.md</code> does not run on its own, it loads once the model calls <code>Skill</code>.</p>
<h3>skill</h3>
<p>A skill is a <code>SKILL.md</code>, at <code>.claude/skills/&#x3C;name>/SKILL.md</code>. Put it under a project directory and only that project loads it; put it under <code>~/.claude/skills/</code> and every project does.</p>
<p>The block between the two <code>---</code> lines at the top is the frontmatter, YAML, and every setting goes there. Below the second <code>---</code> are the instructions for the model.</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: hooktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then report in one line exactly what happened.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The model reads <code>description</code> to decide when to use it. The body is what it follows once loaded. <code>SKILL.md</code> is just text and never runs on its own.</p>
<h3>agent</h3>
<p>An agent definition gives you a subagent, a context without the main line's conversation history, that takes a task, finishes it, and hands a summary back. The steps in between never reach the main thread.</p>
<p>The CLI and the SDK keep the definition in different places:</p>
<ul>
<li>the CLI reads a file, <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code></li>
<li>the SDK has no file layer. The entry point for running a session is <code>query()</code>, and the same content goes in as its <code>agents</code> option, with the same fields the file has</li>
</ul>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: probe</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test agent for preloaded skills and tool limits.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">skills: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#DBEDFF;--shiki-dark-text-decoration:underline;--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-light-text-decoration:underline">secretskill</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">tools: [Read, Bash]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">model: haiku</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">You are a test agent. Answer exactly what is asked.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <code>tools</code> line sets the subagent's tool list:</p>
<ul>
<li>leave it out and it inherits the parent agent's list, whatever the parent has</li>
<li>write it and it can only use the ones declared</li>
<li>for it to open a level of its own, the list has to include <code>Agent</code> (<code>Task</code> works too, the engine treats them as one)</li>
</ul>
<p>Two definitions differ only in whether <code>Bash</code> is on the list, both told to run <code>echo HELLO</code>:</p>

















<table><thead><tr><th>What the definition says</th><th>What came back</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>tools: [Read]</code></td><td>echo never runs, <code>tool_uses: 0</code>. The subagent answers <code>I don't have access to a Bash tool. The only available tool I have is the Read function for reading files from the filesystem. I cannot execute shell commands.</code> (verbatim; the model writes this sentence itself and it changes every time)</td></tr><tr><td><code>tools: [Read, Bash]</code></td><td>calls Bash, gets <code>HELLO</code> back</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Another field, <code>skills</code>: write <code>skills: [inner]</code> and the engine only preloads <code>inner</code>'s body into the subagent's context; the subagent's tool list still has no <code>Skill</code> tool, so it cannot invoke any skill. A subagent defined with <code>skills: [inner]</code> and <code>tools: [Read, Bash]</code> reports that it has no <code>Skill</code> tool, only <code>Read</code> and <code>Bash</code>, yet it can tell you what <code>inner</code>'s body asks for, because that text is already in its context.</p>
<h4>tools, skills, allowedTools, disallowedTools</h4>
<p>Throughout, capital <code>Skill</code> is the tool on the tool list and lowercase skill is the <code>SKILL.md</code> on disk.</p>





















<table><thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>What writing it does</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>tools</code></td><td>replaces the tool list with what you list, MCP tools included; leave the line out and it inherits the parent's</td></tr><tr><td><code>skills</code></td><td>puts the skill body into the context, tool list untouched</td></tr><tr><td><code>disallowedTools</code></td><td>removes what you list from the tool list, MCP tools included</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>The same names can also be passed to the SDK's <code>query()</code>. <code>disallowedTools</code> behaves the same in <code>query()</code>; <code>tools</code> and <code>skills</code> do not, and <code>query()</code> adds <code>allowedTools</code>:</p>





















<table><thead><tr><th>SDK's <code>query()</code></th><th>What writing it does</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>tools</code></td><td>replaces the built-in tools only, MCP tools left alone</td></tr><tr><td><code>skills</code></td><td>an allowlist; <code>Skill</code> can call only the skills you list</td></tr><tr><td><code>allowedTools</code></td><td>tool list untouched, the tools you list run without asking the user</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>The array quoting splits the same way: <code>query()</code> takes a JS object, so <code>["Read","Bash"]</code> is required; an agent definition is YAML, and this article always writes <code>[Read, Bash]</code>.</p>
<p>Spelling it <code>tools: [Read, Bash, Skill]</code> is marked deprecated (the <code>sdk.d.ts</code> comment: <code>passing 'Skill' here is deprecated — use the skills field instead</code>). But <code>skills</code> in the same type is defined as <code>Array of skill names to preload into the agent context</code>, and preloading into the context is not the same as reaching the tool list: rewrite it as <code>skills: [inner]</code>, ask the subagent to run <code>inner</code> with <code>Skill</code> (the prompt tells it to answer <code>NO-SKILL-TOOL</code> if it has no such tool), and it answers <code>NO-SKILL-TOOL</code>. For a subagent to run a skill, either leave the <code>tools:</code> line out (inheriting the parent's list) or put <code>Skill</code> in it, and those are the only two ways.</p>
<h3>hook</h3>
<p>A hook is one rule in <code>settings.json</code>: which event, what the matcher matches, what runs.</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">    "PreToolUse"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">      "matcher"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Write|Edit"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">      "hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"bash ~/hooks/prose-guard.sh"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    }]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>hooks</code> appears twice in that JSON. The outer one is the event table, with event names like <code>PreToolUse</code> under it. The inner array holds what runs on a match, called the action from here on.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-reference">official reference</a> defines 33 events. The common ones:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>PreToolUse</code> runs before a tool and can deny the call</li>
<li><code>PostToolUse</code> runs after a tool succeeds</li>
<li><code>UserPromptSubmit</code> runs after the prompt is submitted and before the model reads it</li>
<li><code>SessionStart</code> runs once at the start</li>
<li><code>Stop</code> runs when a turn ends</li>
</ul>
<p>The matcher is compared against the tool name: if it contains only letters, digits, <code>_</code>, <code>-</code> and <code>|</code>, it is an exact match; any other character makes it a regex. Empty or <code>*</code> matches everything on that event. Break the regex and the engine does not stop; it prints <code>Invalid regex pattern in hook matcher</code> and counts it as no match. An MCP name has to be written out in full: <code>mcp__jira</code> matches nothing, <code>mcp__jira__.*</code> is the working form.</p>
<p>To do something before every subagent launch, put <code>Agent</code> in the matcher:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"PreToolUse"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"matcher"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Agent"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">    "hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"bash ~/hooks/log-subagent.sh"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }] }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">] } }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <code>type</code> field on each item of the inner <code>hooks</code> array takes one of five values; those are the five actions. The engine runs all five itself; the main-line model takes no part. <code>prompt</code> and <code>agent</code> do make one extra model call, but that is a call the hook makes on its own, separate from the model on the main line.</p>



































<table><thead><tr><th>type</th><th>what runs</th><th>who carries it out</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>command</code></td><td>a shell command, hook input on stdin</td><td>the engine starts a process</td></tr><tr><td><code>prompt</code></td><td>a small model deciding whether a condition holds</td><td>the engine makes one model call</td></tr><tr><td><code>agent</code></td><td>an agent deciding, <code>model</code> selectable, Haiku if you leave it out</td><td>the engine opens a subagent</td></tr><tr><td><code>mcp_tool</code></td><td>a tool on an MCP server you already configured</td><td>the engine sends <code>tools/call</code> to that server</td></tr><tr><td><code>http</code></td><td>a POST of the hook input to a URL</td><td>the engine sends an HTTP request</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Not all five were tested: <code>command</code>, <code>mcp_tool</code> and <code>prompt</code> all ran; <code>agent</code> ran only on tool events; <code>http</code> not at all. The built-in <code>/goal</code> is a <code>prompt</code> on <code>Stop</code>, ending every turn with a <code>Stop hook feedback: [...]</code> line pushed back into the context.</p>
<p>Of the five, only <code>mcp_tool</code> names a tool, in the registered sense from the Tool section above, as in <code>"server": "marker", "tool": "record"</code> (<code>marker</code> is a test MCP server I set up with a single tool called <code>record</code>). The other four name a script path, a prompt, a prompt plus a model, and a URL; the engine handles those itself and they leave no <code>tool_use</code> in the log. The <code>matcher</code> field also holds a tool name, but that one is the condition, not the thing being run.</p>
<h2>The sixteen combinations</h2>
<p>The middle column says who issues the call, and after the arrow is the field that decides whether the route holds. The agent column says subagent, because what was tested is the layer a <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code> opens, and the main line calling a tool itself is not in the table.</p>



































<table><thead><tr><th>Marker</th><th>Which field</th><th>Why it is the one issuing</th><th>Rows</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>engine</strong></td><td><code>agent</code>, <code>mcp_tool</code>, <code>context: fork</code>, <code>hooks:</code></td><td>the field already says who to call and with what arguments</td><td>5 (<code>hooks:</code> alone accounts for two)</td></tr><tr><td><strong>model</strong></td><td><code>tools:</code>, <code>allowed-tools</code></td><td>says only what may be used, not which call</td><td>4</td></tr><tr><td><strong>indirect</strong></td><td>no field at all</td><td>the request goes into the context as text, and the model may or may not act on it</td><td>3</td></tr><tr><td><strong>not possible</strong></td><td>a tool has no config of its own</td><td>a skill and a subagent each have an <code>.md</code>, a hook lives in <code>settings.json</code> or frontmatter; a tool is just a name on the list</td><td>4</td></tr></tbody></table>


























































































<table><thead><tr><th>Caller and target</th><th>Issued by</th><th>What came back</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>subagent calls subagent</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code> including
