<code>hooks:</code></td><td>returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code> (workspace must be trusted)</td></tr><tr><td>subagent calls tool</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code></td><td>leave it out and it matches the parent; <code>tools: [Read]</code> leaves it with Read only</td></tr><tr><td>subagent calls skill</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code> including <code>Skill</code>, or no <code>tools:</code> line</td><td>a <code>tool_use</code> named <code>Skill</code>, whose <code>parent_tool_use_id</code> points at the first level</td></tr><tr><td>hook calls subagent</td><td>engine ← an <code>agent</code> action</td><td><code>Agent hook condition was not met: AGENT-HOOK-BLOCKED</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>hook calls hook</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td>the model inside an <code>agent</code> action calls a tool, which fires it again</td></tr><tr><td>hook calls tool</td><td>engine ← an <code>mcp_tool</code> action</td><td>the MCP server receives the <code>tools/call</code>, with no <code>tool_use</code> in the log</td></tr><tr><td><strong>hook calls skill</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td><code>additionalContext</code> asks the model to call it, ends at <code>GREET-RAN</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls subagent</td><td>engine ← <code>context: fork</code></td><td><code>Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls hook</td><td>engine ← frontmatter <code>hooks:</code></td><td>returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls tool</td><td>model ← <code>allowed-tools</code> does not hold it</td><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code> is declared and the body still gets Bash</td></tr><tr><td><strong>skill calls skill</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td>the body asks the model to call it, returns <code>INNER-RAN</code></td></tr><tr><td>tool calls subagent</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls skill</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls tool</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls hook</td><td>not possible</td><td>the engine calls the hook around the tool; the tool takes no part</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong>Nested subagents have a ceiling.</strong> The default inside the binary is 3, but the engine also reads a remote flag that overrides it, so the actual ceiling is not necessarily 3; <code>CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH</code> sets it explicitly. Depth counts subagents only: the main line is 0, the first subagent the main line opens is 1, and one that subagent opens is 2.</p>
<p>Set it to 2 and the main line opens A (depth 1) and A opens B (depth 2), both fine; when B goes to open a third level below it, its tool list has no <code>Agent</code> in it. Set it to 1 and it is A's list that is missing it.</p>
<p>B declares <code>tools: [Read, Bash, Agent]</code> in its own definition and the list still has no <code>Agent</code>. Once depth hits the ceiling, the engine removes <code>Agent</code> from the list, whatever the definition says.</p>
<p>What the subagent says about it changes from run to run, because the model writes that sentence itself; it is not a fixed engine string. Two runs of the same setup gave <code>no Agent or Task tool available. The only tools in my toolset are Read and Bash</code> and <code>the Agent tool is not available to me</code>.</p>
<h3>Can a tool call anything itself</h3>
<p>tool calls subagent, tool calls skill, tool calls tool: none of these three holds. A tool never issues a call; the caller is the model or the engine.</p>
<p>The subagent that comes up when <code>Agent</code> is called goes on to call things of its own, but that is the subagent calling, not the name <code>Agent</code>.</p>
<p>The engine has no such path for any of the three. There is one way around it: an MCP server is a program someone wrote, so once <code>tools/call</code> arrives it can start a separate <code>claude</code> process, whose engine can open subagents and run skills as usual. The test server has a tool called <code>delegate</code>, and it is one line:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="javascript" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="javascript" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">execFileSync</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"claude"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"-p"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, args.q, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"--output-format"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"text"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">])</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>It returns <code>delegated-agent said: DELEGATED-OK</code>. But that is a separate session, already outside what "who calls who" is asking; it is in here only because it looks so similar. Those three rows stay not possible.</p>
<p><code>tool calls hook</code> fails for a different reason than the three above. The hook does run, but it runs before Bash starts, the engine is what calls it, and Bash takes no part from start to finish:</p>
<pre><code>model writes a tool_use, name=Bash, command=echo MAIN
→ engine checks the hook settings in settings.json
→ the matcher hits, the engine runs that action and waits for it to finish
→ deny     → it stops here, the shell never receives anything
→ no deny  → only now does the engine hand echo MAIN to a shell
</code></pre>
<p>For "tool calls hook" to hold, Bash would have to trigger something while running, and it has not started running. <code>PostToolUse</code> is the same: after Bash finishes, the thing that fires the hook is still the engine.</p>
<h3>When a hook calls a hook or a skill</h3>
<h4>hook calls hook</h4>
<p>None of the five action types takes another hook as its value, so there is nowhere in the settings file to write "and then fire that hook".</p>
<p>Have the model call a tool and it fires again. Two actions off one <code>PreToolUse</code>: a <code>command</code> that writes the matched command into <code>ran.txt</code>, and an <code>agent</code> telling the subagent it opens to run <code>echo FROMHOOKAGENT</code> itself. The main line calls Bash exactly once and <code>ran.txt</code> comes back with two lines:</p>
<pre><code>PreToolUse | echo MAIN
PreToolUse | echo FROMHOOKAGENT
</code></pre>
<p>The second line is that subagent's own call. It declares no hooks, but when it calls Bash the engine checks the same <code>settings.json</code>, and <code>matcher: "Bash"</code> matches a second time.</p>
<p>Change the <code>agent</code> prompt to "reply with the single word OK, no commands needed" and nothing else, and <code>ran.txt</code> comes back with one line. The only variable left is whether the model calls a tool, so whether this route holds is the model's decision.</p>
<p>On that second match the engine runs only the <code>command</code> action and does not process the <code>agent</code> action again, which is why it stops at two lines. In the <code>--debug-file</code> log, <code>Processing agent hook</code> appears only once; when the subagent the hook opened calls Bash, its <code>agent_id</code> is <code>hook-agent-…</code>, the <code>command</code> hook fires as usual, and the <code>agent</code> hook does not. Two runs gave the same result, and the official docs do not mention this. The engine's own calls do not count: an <code>mcp_tool</code> action has the engine call the MCP server directly, the server does receive it, but that call never comes back round to <code>PreToolUse</code>.</p>
<h4>hook calls skill</h4>
<p>None of the five action types takes a skill name as its value.</p>
<p>That leaves the indirect route. The hook script returns <code>additionalContext</code>, that text lands in the model's context, and the model calls the <code>Skill</code> tool itself.</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">echo</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"You must now invoke the skill named greet using the Skill tool before answering."}}'</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Attach it to <code>UserPromptSubmit</code>, type <code>Say hello.</code>, and the next step in the log is a <code>tool_use</code> named <code>Skill</code>, ending at <code>GREET-RAN</code>. This route can also fail. All the hook does is put a sentence into the context; the one that actually calls <code>Skill</code> is the model, and it can ignore the sentence.</p>
<h2>Which fields a skill wires through</h2>
<p>For a skill to bring up a tool, a subagent, or a hook, <code>SKILL.md</code> frontmatter has a field for each: <code>allowed-tools</code> for tools, <code>context: fork</code> plus <code>agent</code> for a subagent, <code>hooks</code> for a hook. <code>context: fork</code> and <code>hooks</code> are things the engine acts on: write them and they happen. <code>allowed-tools</code> is not. What it affects is the step where the skill body calls a tool: for the ones it lists, the engine runs them without asking the user; the body can still call one that is not listed.</p>
<p>When the model calls the <code>Skill</code> tool itself, the engine makes a separate approval decision. Which frontmatter fields make that step need approval? Five skills, each with one field beyond <code>name</code>/<code>description</code>, tested one by one, each invoked once under <code>-p</code>. No <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code>: with it the engine decides allow every time, <code>ask</code> never appears, and there is nothing to measure. Every tool_use gets exactly one <code>tool_result</code> back, whether the skill ran or not; the difference is the string:</p>



































<table><thead><tr><th>skill</th><th>What the frontmatter adds</th><th>What <code>tool_result</code> came back with</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>inner</code></td><td>nothing, <code>name</code> and <code>description</code> only</td><td><code>Launching skill: inner</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>forktest</code></td><td><code>context: fork</code></td><td><code>Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>tooltest</code></td><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: tooltest</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>dtest</code></td><td><code>disallowed-tools: Bash</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: dtest</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>hooktest</code></td><td><code>hooks: PreToolUse …</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: hooktest</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong>The three <code>Execute skill: &#x3C;name></code> rows read as though the skill ran; they are refusals.</strong> The model did send a <code>Skill</code> tool_use, the engine decided it needs approval, nobody can press anything under <code>-p</code>, so it returned a refusal and the body of <code>SKILL.md</code> was never loaded. Run the same <code>tooltest</code> without <code>-p</code> and manual mode shows a dialog reading "Use skill "tooltest"?", while auto mode lets it through; the table in the caveat puts the three modes side by side.</p>
<p>After loading a skill, the engine checks each frontmatter key against a list hardcoded in the binary (44 entries; <code>strings</code> pulls out the <code>new Set(["type","progressMessage"…</code> that holds it, and there is no public document). The common keys fall on two sides:</p>




















<table><thead><tr><th>frontmatter key</th><th>on the list</th><th>what writing it does</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>name</code>, <code>description</code>, <code>model</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>agent</code>, <code>background</code></td><td>yes</td><td>loads straight away, no prompt</td></tr><tr><td><code>hooks</code>, <code>allowed-tools</code>, <code>disallowed-tools</code>, and any key the list does not have</td><td>no</td><td>with something after the colon, the engine asks a person before loading; left empty, <code>[]</code> or <code>{}</code> counts as not written and it loads straight away</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><code>tooltest</code>'s <code>allowed-tools: Read</code> is the second row and gets <code>Execute skill: tooltest</code> back; <code>forktest</code>'s <code>context: fork</code> is the first row and runs straight away.</p>
<p>The comparison uses the loaded object's properties, so <code>allowed-tools</code> becomes <code>allowedTools</code> on the way in; neither spelling is on the list, and the result is the same.</p>
<p>A skill calling another skill has no field at all. No frontmatter key takes another skill's name, so it has to go in the body.</p>
<h3>skill wires to a tool</h3>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: restricttest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test skill. Use when the user says restricttest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">allowed-tools: Read</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then state in one line whether the Bash call succeeded or was refused.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The zod schema inside the binary describes this field as <code>Tools available to the model while this file is active</code>, which reads as though only the listed tools can be used; the actual runs say otherwise. Same body, same question, one run per frontmatter:</p>





















<table><thead><tr><th>What the frontmatter declares</th><th>Does Bash run</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>no such line</td><td>it runs, <code>tool_result</code> comes back <code>HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code></td><td>it runs, <code>tool_result</code> comes back <code>HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>disallowed-tools: Bash</code></td><td><code>Permission to use Bash has been denied.</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>When the skill body calls a tool <code>allowed-tools</code> lists, the engine does not ask the user; unlisted ones can still be called. What does hold is <code>disallowed-tools</code>, described as <code>Tools removed from the model while this file is active</code>, and it holds even under <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code>.</p>
<p>The <code>disallowed-tools</code> description carries one more clause: <code>Cleared when the user sends the next message</code>. <code>--resume</code> the same session with a second message asking for <code>echo AFTER</code>, and Bash comes back with <code>AFTER</code>. The restriction lives only for the turn the skill was called in.</p>
<p>An agent definition has <code>tools</code> and <code>disallowedTools</code>; <code>SKILL.md</code> has no <code>tools</code>. On an agent definition, <code>tools</code> is a whitelist over the whole list and <code>disallowedTools</code> works the other way, removing what it lists and leaving the rest. What each one covers is in the agent section above.</p>
<h3>skill wires to a subagent</h3>
<p>The same skill, one line apart:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  name: forktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  description: Test skill. Use when the user says forktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ context: fork</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  Reply with exactly one word: FORKED</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>With <code>context: fork</code> written, the engine opens a subagent to run the skill. The body becomes that subagent's task. Without <code>context: fork</code>, the body loads into the main line and the model follows it there.</p>
<p>Call each one and the <code>tool_result</code> string differs. <code>-</code> is the version without it, <code>+</code> is the one with <code>context: fork</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#FDAEB7;--shiki-light:#B31D28">- Launching skill: forktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ Result:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ FORKED</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The companion field <code>agent</code> picks which agent type runs it, and takes the name from a <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code> or a built-in type such as <code>Explore</code>. It is optional: <code>context: fork</code> on its own still forks. A name that does not exist raises nothing; see "Silent failures" below.</p>
<h3>skill wires to a hook</h3>
<p>Give the skill's <code>hooks:</code> a script that always denies Bash, and have the body ask Bash to run <code>echo HELLO</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: hooktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">hooks:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  PreToolUse:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    - matcher: Bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">      hooks:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">        - type: command</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">          command: bash .claude/skills/hooktest/deny.sh</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then report in one line exactly what happened.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>One line of JSON in <code>deny.sh</code> is enough:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">echo</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK"}}'</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>With <code>permissionDecision</code> set to <code>deny</code>, the engine never hands <code>echo HELLO</code> to the shell. The <code>permissionDecisionReason</code> string becomes the <code>tool_result</code> the model reads, so what the model sees is <code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code>.</p>
<p>To see when the deny starts applying and when it stops, three prompts go in a row in one session. <code>echo BEFORE</code> and <code>echo AFTER</code> are not in <code>hooktest</code>'s <code>SKILL.md</code>; they are typed separately:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>Input</th><th>What came back</th><th>Where things stand</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>echo BEFORE</code></td><td><code>BEFORE</code></td><td>the skill has not been invoked yet</td></tr><tr><td><code>hooktest</code></td><td><code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td><td>what got blocked is the body's <code>echo HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>echo AFTER</code></td><td><code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td><td>the skill has already finished</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>So its scope is "absent until the skill is invoked, present from then on", not "only while that skill runs". It goes away with the session: open a new one in the same directory, run <code>echo AFTER</code>, and it comes back as <code>AFTER</code>.</p>
<h4>For comparison: agent wires to a hook</h4>
<p>An agent definition's frontmatter supports <code>hooks:</code> too, with the same fields as in <code>SKILL.md</code>. Copy the same deny rule into <code>.claude/agents/probe.md</code>, ask probe to run <code>echo SUB</code>, and back comes <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code>. The same three messages in one session:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>input</th><th>what comes back</th><th>state at that moment</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>echo BEFORE</code> (main line)</td><td><code>BEFORE</code></td><td>probe not opened yet</td></tr><tr><td>tell probe to run <code>echo SUB</code></td><td><code>PreToolUse:Bash hook error: BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code></td><td>probe's <code>hooks:</code> active inside the subagent</td></tr><tr><td><code>echo AFTER</code> (main line)</td><td><code>AFTER</code></td><td>main line untouched</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>The difference from the skill table is the third row: a skill's <code>hooks:</code> stays on the session once it has run, so the main line's <code>echo AFTER</code> is refused too; an agent's lives only inside the subagent, and the main line runs as usual. A second difference shows in an untrusted folder: the engine drops <code>probe.md</code>'s <code>hooks:</code> wholesale and <code>echo SUB</code> comes back as <code>SUB</code>, while <code>SKILL.md</code>'s registers as usual and <code>echo HELLO</code> still comes back as <code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code>. The silent failures section has the comparison.</p>
<h3>skill wires to another skill</h3>
<p>No field for this one, so it goes in the body:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: outer</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Outer test skill. Use when the user says outer.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Invoke the skill named inner using the Skill tool. Then reply with whatever it returned.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>inner</code> replies with the single word <code>INNER-RAN</code>. Type <code>outer</code> and the log holds two <code>Skill</code> calls:</p>
<pre><code>TOOL_USE: Skill {"skill": "outer"}
TOOL_USE: Skill {"skill": "inner"}
RESULT: INNER-RAN
</code></pre>
<p>The second call comes from the model, not the engine. Same as a hook reaching for a skill: if the model does not follow the instruction, nothing happens.</p>
<h2>Silent failures</h2>
<p>Three places above mentioned a setting that fails without an error: the event name in the hook section, the <code>agent</code> value in skill wires to a subagent, and trust in agent wires to a hook. All three run exactly as they do when written right, with no error message. To catch them, you can only list what a correct setup would produce and then check whether it appeared.</p>





























<table><thead><tr><th>What is wrong</th><th>Expected result when correct</th><th>What the wrong one shows</th><th>Any hint</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>event name <code>PreToolUsee</code> in <code>settings.json</code>, one e too many</td><td><code>--include-hook-events</code> adds <code>hook_started</code> and <code>hook_response</code></td><td>neither appears, Bash runs anyway</td><td>none; neither <code>--debug</code> (debug log on stderr) nor <code>--include-hook-events</code> (hook events in stream-json) prints a line about it</td></tr><tr><td><code>agent: nosuchagent</code> on a skill</td><td><code>agent: mycustom</code> returns <code>CUSTOM: FORKED</code></td><td>returns <code>FORKED</code>, forking with the default agent</td><td>none</td></tr><tr><td>folder not trusted</td><td><code>deny.sh</code> gets its own <code>hook_started</code> and <code>hook_response</code>, <code>echo SUB</code> returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code></td><td>no events at all, <code>echo SUB</code> returns <code>SUB</code>; the <code>hooks:</code> in the agent's frontmatter are dropped wholesale</td><td>none; <code>-p</code> never shows the trust dialog and <code>--debug</code> says nothing</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Trust is asked once per folder: the first interactive session started there puts up a dialog, and the answer is stored as <code>hasTrustDialogAccepted</code> in <code>~/.claude.json</code>. Under <code>-p</code> that dialog never appears.</p>
<h2>caveat</h2>
<p>The CLI and the SDK execute the same binary (<code>shasum</code> matches). What the SDK adds is that <code>agents</code>, <code>mcpServers</code> and hook callbacks can be passed straight as options, and <code>tools</code> and <code>skills</code> behave differently in <code>query()</code> (see the <code>query()</code> table above). For the nesting ceiling the engine also reads a remote flag, so it may move without a version change.</p>
<p>Every measurement in this article ran with <code>-p</code>. <code>-p</code> changes two results: <code>tooltest</code> returns <code>Execute skill: tooltest</code> because under <code>-p</code> nobody answers the ask; <code>forktest</code>'s result comes straight back to the main line because <code>-p</code> does not push the subagent into the background. The same two skills, rerun in the other two modes:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>Mode</th><th>A skill with <code>allowed-tools</code></th><th><code>context: fork</code></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>--permission-mode manual</code></td><td>a real dialog, <code>Use skill "tooltest"?</code></td><td>the subagent runs in the background, the main line does not wait for it, and <code>FORKED</code> arrives later; add <code>background: false</code> to the frontmatter and the main line waits</td></tr><tr><td>default auto mode</td><td>asks nothing, logs <code>Allowed by auto mode classifier</code></td><td>same</td></tr><tr><td><code>-p</code></td><td>nobody to ask, comes back as <code>Execute skill: tooltest</code></td><td>no background: the subagent finishes and <code>FORKED</code> comes straight back to the main line</td></tr></tbody></table>16:T769e,
I wanted to know whether these things nest, one inside another like a matryoshka doll, so I tried it. Claude Code lets you configure four: skills, agents, tools, hooks. Pair them up and you get sixteen combinations. I ran all sixteen.

- `allowed-tools` lists Read and nothing else, the skill body triggers Bash, and Bash runs anyway even though it is not on the list
- Once you invoke a skill carrying `hooks:`, that hook stays for the rest of the session. It does not go away when the skill finishes
- One extra `e` in a hook's event name in `settings.json`, `PreToolUsee`: no error, no trigger. Add `--debug` or `--include-hook-events` to check and there is still no error message, only the hook events that should have been there are missing

Environment:

- CLI 2.1.257, invoked as `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.257` every time, never through the `claude` symlink, which updates itself
- Agent SDK pinned at 0.3.257
- every run under `-p` (`--print`): one prompt in, the result printed, then exit, with no interactive session and no dialogs

## model and engine

The `model` is Opus, Fable and the rest: the language model reached over the API. When it wants to call a tool, its reply carries an extra `tool_use` block:

```json
{"type": "tool_use", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "git status"}}
```

That JSON is text the model wrote. `git status` has not run at this point.

The `engine` is the `claude` binary running locally. It hands the tool list to the model, runs whatever `tool_use` comes back, and on either side of that run checks `settings.json` for hooks.

Every separate context the engine spins up to get something done is a subagent. The main line counts as one too. Each context has its own tool list: one for the main line, one for each subagent.

Of the four primitives below, skills and agents are `.md` files on disk, hooks live in `settings.json` or frontmatter, and tools have no file at all. They do nothing on their own; the behaviour comes from the model and the engine reading them.

## The four

### tool

A tool is a function the model can call. A name and a parameter schema, nothing else.

The list has `Bash` on it and no `git status`. Ask the model to run `git status` and what it issues is one `Bash` call, with `git status` as the argument. To be a tool, a thing has to be registered in this session's tool list; unregistered, the model cannot see it and cannot call it.

A tool on that list is not itself a process. `Bash` is a name plus an argument shape, and the command only reaches a shell once the tool is called.

Built-in tool names are single words: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`.

MCP servers hand you this format:

- `mcp__<server>__<tool>`
- `mcp__claude_ai_Jira__getJiraIssue`

Capitalised, `Agent` and `Skill` are tools as well, sitting on the same list as `Bash` and `Read`; lowercase, agent and skill are `.md` files on disk, saying who the agent plays or what steps the skill follows. Starting a subagent is the model calling `Agent`; running a skill is the model calling `Skill`. A `SKILL.md` does not run on its own, it loads once the model calls `Skill`.

### skill

A skill is a `SKILL.md`, at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Put it under a project directory and only that project loads it; put it under `~/.claude/skills/` and every project does.

The block between the two `---` lines at the top is the frontmatter, YAML, and every setting goes there. Below the second `---` are the instructions for the model.

```markdown
---
name: hooktest
description: Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.
---

Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO
Then report in one line exactly what happened.
```

The model reads `description` to decide when to use it. The body is what it follows once loaded. `SKILL.md` is just text and never runs on its own.

### agent

An agent definition gives you a subagent, a context without the main line's conversation history, that takes a task, finishes it, and hands a summary back. The steps in between never reach the main thread.

The CLI and the SDK keep the definition in different places:

- the CLI reads a file, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- the SDK has no file layer. The entry point for running a session is `query()`, and the same content goes in as its `agents` option, with the same fields the file has

```markdown
---
name: probe
description: Test agent for preloaded skills and tool limits.
skills: [secretskill]
tools: [Read, Bash]
model: haiku
---

You are a test agent. Answer exactly what is asked.
```

The `tools` line sets the subagent's tool list:

- leave it out and it inherits the parent agent's list, whatever the parent has
- write it and it can only use the ones declared
- for it to open a level of its own, the list has to include `Agent` (`Task` works too, the engine treats them as one)

Two definitions differ only in whether `Bash` is on the list, both told to run `echo HELLO`:

| What the definition says | What came back |
|---|---|
| `tools: [Read]` | echo never runs, `tool_uses: 0`. The subagent answers `I don't have access to a Bash tool. The only available tool I have is the Read function for reading files from the filesystem. I cannot execute shell commands.` (verbatim; the model writes this sentence itself and it changes every time) |
| `tools: [Read, Bash]` | calls Bash, gets `HELLO` back |

Another field, `skills`: write `skills: [inner]` and the engine only preloads `inner`'s body into the subagent's context; the subagent's tool list still has no `Skill` tool, so it cannot invoke any skill. A subagent defined with `skills: [inner]` and `tools: [Read, Bash]` reports that it has no `Skill` tool, only `Read` and `Bash`, yet it can tell you what `inner`'s body asks for, because that text is already in its context.

#### tools, skills, allowedTools, disallowedTools

Throughout, capital `Skill` is the tool on the tool list and lowercase skill is the `SKILL.md` on disk.

| Field | What writing it does |
|---|---|
| `tools` | replaces the tool list with what you list, MCP tools included; leave the line out and it inherits the parent's |
| `skills` | puts the skill body into the context, tool list untouched |
| `disallowedTools` | removes what you list from the tool list, MCP tools included |

The same names can also be passed to the SDK's `query()`. `disallowedTools` behaves the same in `query()`; `tools` and `skills` do not, and `query()` adds `allowedTools`:

| SDK's `query()` | What writing it does |
|---|---|
| `tools` | replaces the built-in tools only, MCP tools left alone |
| `skills` | an allowlist; `Skill` can call only the skills you list |
| `allowedTools` | tool list untouched, the tools you list run without asking the user |

The array quoting splits the same way: `query()` takes a JS object, so `["Read","Bash"]` is required; an agent definition is YAML, and this article always writes `[Read, Bash]`.

Spelling it `tools: [Read, Bash, Skill]` is marked deprecated (the `sdk.d.ts` comment: `passing 'Skill' here is deprecated — use the skills field instead`). But `skills` in the same type is defined as `Array of skill names to preload into the agent context`, and preloading into the context is not the same as reaching the tool list: rewrite it as `skills: [inner]`, ask the subagent to run `inner` with `Skill` (the prompt tells it to answer `NO-SKILL-TOOL` if it has no such tool), and it answers `NO-SKILL-TOOL`. For a subagent to run a skill, either leave the `tools:` line out (inheriting the parent's list) or put `Skill` in it, and those are the only two ways.

### hook

A hook is one rule in `settings.json`: which event, what the matcher matches, what runs.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "bash ~/hooks/prose-guard.sh" }]
    }]
  }
}
```

`hooks` appears twice in that JSON. The outer one is the event table, with event names like `PreToolUse` under it. The inner array holds what runs on a match, called the action from here on.

The [official reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-reference) defines 33 events. The common ones:

- `PreToolUse` runs before a tool and can deny the call
- `PostToolUse` runs after a tool succeeds
- `UserPromptSubmit` runs after the prompt is submitted and before the model reads it
- `SessionStart` runs once at the start
- `Stop` runs when a turn ends

The matcher is compared against the tool name: if it contains only letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `|`, it is an exact match; any other character makes it a regex. Empty or `*` matches everything on that event. Break the regex and the engine does not stop; it prints `Invalid regex pattern in hook matcher` and counts it as no match. An MCP name has to be written out in full: `mcp__jira` matches nothing, `mcp__jira__.*` is the working form.

To do something before every subagent launch, put `Agent` in the matcher:

```json
{ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [
  { "matcher": "Agent",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "bash ~/hooks/log-subagent.sh" }] }
] } }
```

The `type` field on each item of the inner `hooks` array takes one of five values; those are the five actions. The engine runs all five itself; the main-line model takes no part. `prompt` and `agent` do make one extra model call, but that is a call the hook makes on its own, separate from the model on the main line.

| type | what runs | who carries it out |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | a shell command, hook input on stdin | the engine starts a process |
| `prompt` | a small model deciding whether a condition holds | the engine makes one model call |
| `agent` | an agent deciding, `model` selectable, Haiku if you leave it out | the engine opens a subagent |
| `mcp_tool` | a tool on an MCP server you already configured | the engine sends `tools/call` to that server |
| `http` | a POST of the hook input to a URL | the engine sends an HTTP request |

Not all five were tested: `command`, `mcp_tool` and `prompt` all ran; `agent` ran only on tool events; `http` not at all. The built-in `/goal` is a `prompt` on `Stop`, ending every turn with a `Stop hook feedback: [...]` line pushed back into the context.

Of the five, only `mcp_tool` names a tool, in the registered sense from the Tool section above, as in `"server": "marker", "tool": "record"` (`marker` is a test MCP server I set up with a single tool called `record`). The other four name a script path, a prompt, a prompt plus a model, and a URL; the engine handles those itself and they leave no `tool_use` in the log. The `matcher` field also holds a tool name, but that one is the condition, not the thing being run.

## The sixteen combinations

The middle column says who issues the call, and after the arrow is the field that decides whether the route holds. The agent column says subagent, because what was tested is the layer a `.claude/agents/<name>.md` opens, and the main line calling a tool itself is not in the table.

| Marker | Which field | Why it is the one issuing | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **engine** | `agent`, `mcp_tool`, `context: fork`, `hooks:` | the field already says who to call and with what arguments | 5 (`hooks:` alone accounts for two) |
| **model** | `tools:`, `allowed-tools` | says only what may be used, not which call | 4 |
| **indirect** | no field at all | the request goes into the context as text, and the model may or may not act on it | 3 |
| **not possible** | a tool has no config of its own | a skill and a subagent each have an `.md`, a hook lives in `settings.json` or frontmatter; a tool is just a name on the list | 4 |

| Caller and target | Issued by | What came back |
|---|---|---|
| subagent calls subagent | model ← `tools:` including `Agent` | the second-level `tool_use` carries the first level's `parent_tool_use_id` |
| subagent calls hook | engine ← frontmatter `hooks:` | returns `BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK` (workspace must be trusted) |
| subagent calls tool | model ← `tools:` | leave it out and it matches the parent; `tools: [Read]` leaves it with Read only |
| subagent calls skill | model ← `tools:` including `Skill`, or no `tools:` line | a `tool_use` named `Skill`, whose `parent_tool_use_id` points at the first level |
| hook calls subagent | engine ← an `agent` action | `Agent hook condition was not met: AGENT-HOOK-BLOCKED` |
| **hook calls hook** | indirect model ← no field | the model inside an `agent` action calls a tool, which fires it again |
| hook calls tool | engine ← an `mcp_tool` action | the MCP server receives the `tools/call`, with no `tool_use` in the log |
| **hook calls skill** | indirect model ← no field | `additionalContext` asks the model to call it, ends at `GREET-RAN` |
| skill calls subagent | engine ← `context: fork` | `Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).` |
| skill calls hook | engine ← frontmatter `hooks:` | returns `BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK` |
| skill calls tool | model ← `allowed-tools` does not hold it | `allowed-tools: Read` is declared and the body still gets Bash |
| **skill calls skill** | indirect model ← no field | the body asks the model to call it, returns `INNER-RAN` |
| tool calls subagent | not possible | no such path in the engine |
| tool calls skill | not possible | no such path in the engine |
| tool calls tool | not possible | no such path in the engine |
| tool calls hook | not possible | the engine calls the hook around the tool; the tool takes no part |

**Nested subagents have a ceiling.** The default inside the binary is 3, but the engine also reads a remote flag that overrides it, so the actual ceiling is not necessarily 3; `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` sets it explicitly. Depth counts subagents only: the main line is 0, the first subagent the main line opens is 1, and one that subagent opens is 2.

Set it to 2 and the main line opens A (depth 1) and A opens B (depth 2), both fine; when B goes to open a third level below it, its tool list has no `Agent` in it. Set it to 1 and it is A's list that is missing it.

B declares `tools: [Read, Bash, Agent]` in its own definition and the list still has no `Agent`. Once depth hits the ceiling, the engine removes `Agent` from the list, whatever the definition says.

What the subagent says about it changes from run to run, because the model writes that sentence itself; it is not a fixed engine string. Two runs of the same setup gave `no Agent or Task tool available. The only tools in my toolset are Read and Bash` and `the Agent tool is not available to me`.

### Can a tool call anything itself

tool calls subagent, tool calls skill, tool calls tool: none of these three holds. A tool never issues a call; the caller is the model or the engine.

The subagent that comes up when `Agent` is called goes on to call things of its own, but that is the subagent calling, not the name `Agent`.

The engine has no such path for any of the three. There is one way around it: an MCP server is a program someone wrote, so once `tools/call` arrives it can start a separate `claude` process, whose engine can open subagents and run skills as usual. The test server has a tool called `delegate`, and it is one line:

```javascript
execFileSync("claude", ["-p", args.q, "--output-format", "text"])
```

It returns `delegated-agent said: DELEGATED-OK`. But that is a separate session, already outside what "who calls who" is asking; it is in here only because it looks so similar. Those three rows stay not possible.

`tool calls hook` fails for a different reason than the three above. The hook does run, but it runs before Bash starts, the engine is what calls it, and Bash takes no part from start to finish:

```
model writes a tool_use, name=Bash, command=echo MAIN
→ engine checks the hook settings in settings.json
→ the matcher hits, the engine runs that action and waits for it to finish
→ deny     → it stops here, the shell never receives anything
→ no deny  → only now does the engine hand echo MAIN to a shell
```

For "tool calls hook" to hold, Bash would have to trigger something while running, and it has not started running. `PostToolUse` is the same: after Bash finishes, the thing that fires the hook is still the engine.

### When a hook calls a hook or a skill

#### hook calls hook

None of the five action types takes another hook as its value, so there is nowhere in the settings file to write "and then fire that hook".

Have the model call a tool and it fires again. Two actions off one `PreToolUse`: a `command` that writes the matched command into `ran.txt`, and an `agent` telling the subagent it opens to run `echo FROMHOOKAGENT` itself. The main line calls Bash exactly once and `ran.txt` comes back with two lines:

```
PreToolUse | echo MAIN
PreToolUse | echo FROMHOOKAGENT
```

The second line is that subagent's own call. It declares no hooks, but when it calls Bash the engine checks the same `settings.json`, and `matcher: "Bash"` matches a second time.

Change the `agent` prompt to "reply with the single word OK, no commands needed" and nothing else, and `ran.txt` comes back with one line. The only variable left is whether the model calls a tool, so whether this route holds is the model's decision.

On that second match the engine runs only the `command` action and does not process the `agent` action again, which is why it stops at two lines. In the `--debug-file` log, `Processing agent hook` appears only once; when the subagent the hook opened calls Bash, its `agent_id` is `hook-agent-…`, the `command` hook fires as usual, and the `agent` hook does not. Two runs gave the same result, and the official docs do not mention this. The engine's own calls do not count: an `mcp_tool` action has the engine call the MCP server directly, the server does receive it, but that call never comes back round to `PreToolUse`.

#### hook calls skill

None of the five action types takes a skill name as its value.

That leaves the indirect route. The hook script returns `additionalContext`, that text lands in the model's context, and the model calls the `Skill` tool itself.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"You must now invoke the skill named greet using the Skill tool before answering."}}'
```

Attach it to `UserPromptSubmit`, type `Say hello.`, and the next step in the log is a `tool_use` named `Skill`, ending at `GREET-RAN`. This route can also fail. All the hook does is put a sentence into the context; the one that actually calls `Skill` is the model, and it can ignore the sentence.

## Which fields a skill wires through

For a skill to bring up a tool, a subagent, or a hook, `SKILL.md` frontmatter has a field for each: `allowed-tools` for tools, `context: fork` plus `agent` for a subagent, `hooks` for a hook. `context: fork` and `hooks` are things the engine acts on: write them and they happen. `allowed-tools` is not. What it affects is the step where the skill body calls a tool: for the ones it lists, the engine runs them without asking the user; the body can still call one that is not listed.

When the model calls the `Skill` tool itself, the engine makes a separate approval decision. Which frontmatter fields make that step need approval? Five skills, each with one field beyond `name`/`description`, tested one by one, each invoked once under `-p`. No `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: with it the engine decides allow every time, `ask` never appears, and there is nothing to measure. Every tool_use gets exactly one `tool_result` back, whether the skill ran or not; the difference is the string:

| skill | What the frontmatter adds | What `tool_result` came back with |
|---|---|---|
| `inner` | nothing, `name` and `description` only | `Launching skill: inner` |
| `forktest` | `context: fork` | `Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).` |
| `tooltest` | `allowed-tools: Read` | `Execute skill: tooltest` |
| `dtest` | `disallowed-tools: Bash` | `Execute skill: dtest` |
| `hooktest` | `hooks: PreToolUse …` | `Execute skill: hooktest` |

**The three `Execute skill: <name>` rows read as though the skill ran; they are refusals.** The model did send a `Skill` tool_use, the engine decided it needs approval, nobody can press anything under `-p`, so it returned a refusal and the body of `SKILL.md` was never loaded. Run the same `tooltest` without `-p` and manual mode shows a dialog reading "Use skill "tooltest"?", while auto mode lets it through; the table in the caveat puts the three modes side by side.

After loading a skill, the engine checks each frontmatter key against a list hardcoded in the binary (44 entries; `strings` pulls out the `new Set(["type","progressMessage"…` that holds it, and there is no public document). The common keys fall on two sides:

| frontmatter key | on the list | what writing it does |
|---|---|---|
| `name`, `description`, `model`, `context`, `agent`, `background` | yes | loads straight away, no prompt |
| `hooks`, `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools`, and any key the list does not have | no | with something after the colon, the engine asks a person before loading; left empty, `[]` or `{}` counts as not written and it loads straight away |

`tooltest`'s `allowed-tools: Read` is the second row and gets `Execute skill: tooltest` back; `forktest`'s `context: fork` is the first row and runs straight away.

The comparison uses the loaded object's properties, so `allowed-tools` becomes `allowedTools` on the way in; neither spelling is on the list, and the result is the same.

A skill calling another skill has no field at all. No frontmatter key takes another skill's name, so it has to go in the body.

### skill wires to a tool

```markdown
---
name: restricttest
description: Test skill. Use when the user says restricttest.
allowed-tools: Read
---

Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO
Then state in one line whether the Bash call succeeded or was refused.
```

The zod schema inside the binary describes this field as `Tools available to the model while this file is active`, which reads as though only the listed tools can be used; the actual runs say otherwise. Same body, same question, one run per frontmatter:

| What the frontmatter declares | Does Bash run |
|---|---|
| no such line | it runs, `tool_result` comes back `HELLO` |
| `allowed-tools: Read` | it runs, `tool_result` comes back `HELLO` |
| `disallowed-tools: Bash` | `Permission to use Bash has been denied.` |

When the skill body calls a tool `allowed-tools` lists, the engine does not ask the user; unlisted ones can still be called. What does hold is `disallowed-tools`, described as `Tools removed from the model while this file is active`, and it holds even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

The `disallowed-tools` description carries one more clause: `Cleared when the user sends the next message`. `--resume` the same session with a second message asking for `echo AFTER`, and Bash comes back with `AFTER`. The restriction lives only for the turn the skill was called in.

An agent definition has `tools` and `disallowedTools`; `SKILL.md` has no `tools`. On an agent definition, `tools` is a whitelist over the whole list and `disallowedTools` works the other way, removing what it lists and leaving the rest. What each one covers is in the agent section above.

### skill wires to a subagent

The same skill, one line apart:

```diff
  ---
  name: forktest
  description: Test skill. Use when the user says forktest.
+ context: fork
  ---

  Reply with exactly one word: FORKED
```

With `context: fork` written, the engine opens a subagent to run the skill. The body becomes that subagent's task. Without `context: fork`, the body loads into the main line and the model follows it there.

Call each one and the `tool_result` string differs. `-` is the version without it, `+` is the one with `context: fork`:

```diff
- Launching skill: forktest
+ Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).
+ Result:
+ FORKED
```

The companion field `agent` picks which agent type runs it, and takes the name from a `.claude/agents/<name>.md` or a built-in type such as `Explore`. It is optional: `context: fork` on its own still forks. A name that does not exist raises nothing; see "Silent failures" below.

### skill wires to a hook

Give the skill's `hooks:` a script that always denies Bash, and have the body ask Bash to run `echo HELLO`:

```markdown
---
name: hooktest
description: Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: Bash
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: bash .claude/skills/hooktest/deny.sh
---

Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO
Then report in one line exactly what happened.
```

One line of JSON in `deny.sh` is enough:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK"}}'
```

With `permissionDecision` set to `deny`, the engine never hands `echo HELLO` to the shell. The `permissionDecisionReason` string becomes the `tool_result` the model reads, so what the model sees is `BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK`.

To see when the deny starts applying and when it stops, three prompts go in a row in one session. `echo BEFORE` and `echo AFTER` are not in `hooktest`'s `SKILL.md`; they are typed separately:

| Input | What came back | Where things stand |
|---|---|---|
| `echo BEFORE` | `BEFORE` | the skill has not been invoked yet |
| `hooktest` | `BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK` | what got blocked is the body's `echo HELLO` |
| `echo AFTER` | `BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK` | the skill has already finished |

So its scope is "absent until the skill is invoked, present from then on", not "only while that skill runs". It goes away with the session: open a new one in the same directory, run `echo AFTER`, and it comes back as `AFTER`.

#### For comparison: agent wires to a hook

An agent definition's frontmatter supports `hooks:` too, with the same fields as in `SKILL.md`. Copy the same deny rule into `.claude/agents/probe.md`, ask probe to run `echo SUB`, and back comes `BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK`. The same three messages in one session:

| input | what comes back | state at that moment |
|---|---|---|
| `echo BEFORE` (main line) | `BEFORE` | probe not opened yet |
| tell probe to run `echo SUB` | `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK` | probe's `hooks:` active inside the subagent |
| `echo AFTER` (main line) | `AFTER` | main line untouched |

The difference from the skill table is the third row: a skill's `hooks:` stays on the session once it has run, so the main line's `echo AFTER` is refused too; an agent's lives only inside the subagent, and the main line runs as usual. A second difference shows in an untrusted folder: the engine drops `probe.md`'s `hooks:` wholesale and `echo SUB` comes back as `SUB`, while `SKILL.md`'s registers as usual and `echo HELLO` still comes back as `BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK`. The silent failures section has the comparison.

### skill wires to another skill

No field for this one, so it goes in the body:

```markdown
---
name: outer
description: Outer test skill. Use when the user says outer.
---

Invoke the skill named inner using the Skill tool. Then reply with whatever it returned.
```

`inner` replies with the single word `INNER-RAN`. Type `outer` and the log holds two `Skill` calls:

```
TOOL_USE: Skill {"skill": "outer"}
TOOL_USE: Skill {"skill": "inner"}
RESULT: INNER-RAN
```

The second call comes from the model, not the engine. Same as a hook reaching for a skill: if the model does not follow the instruction, nothing happens.

## Silent failures

Three places above mentioned a setting that fails without an error: the event name in the hook section, the `agent` value in skill wires to a subagent, and trust in agent wires to a hook. All three run exactly as they do when written right, with no error message. To catch them, you can only list what a correct setup would produce and then check whether it appeared.

| What is wrong | Expected result when correct | What the wrong one shows | Any hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| event name `PreToolUsee` in `settings.json`, one e too many | `--include-hook-events` adds `hook_started` and `hook_response` | neither appears, Bash runs anyway | none; neither `--debug` (debug log on stderr) nor `--include-hook-events` (hook events in stream-json) prints a line about it |
| `agent: nosuchagent` on a skill | `agent: mycustom` returns `CUSTOM: FORKED` | returns `FORKED`, forking with the default agent | none |
| folder not trusted | `deny.sh` gets its own `hook_started` and `hook_response`, `echo SUB` returns `BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK` | no events at all, `echo SUB` returns `SUB`; the `hooks:` in the agent's frontmatter are dropped wholesale | none; `-p` never shows the trust dialog and `--debug` says nothing |

Trust is asked once per folder: the first interactive session started there puts up a dialog, and the answer is stored as `hasTrustDialogAccepted` in `~/.claude.json`. Under `-p` that dialog never appears.

## caveat

The CLI and the SDK execute the same binary (`shasum` matches). What the SDK adds is that `agents`, `mcpServers` and hook callbacks can be passed straight as options, and `tools` and `skills` behave differently in `query()` (see the `query()` table above). For the nesting ceiling the engine also reads a remote flag, so it may move without a version change.

Every measurement in this article ran with `-p`. `-p` changes two results: `tooltest` returns `Execute skill: tooltest` because under `-p` nobody answers the ask; `forktest`'s result comes straight back to the main line because `-p` does not push the subagent into the background. The same two skills, rerun in the other two modes:

| Mode | A skill with `allowed-tools` | `context: fork` |
|---|---|---|
| `--permission-mode manual` | a real dialog, `Use skill "tooltest"?` | the subagent runs in the background, the main line does not wait for it, and `FORKED` arrives later; add `background: false` to the frontmatter and the main line waits |
| default auto mode | asks nothing, logs `Allowed by auto mode classifier` | same |
| `-p` | nobody to ask, comes back as `Execute skill: tooltest` | no background: the subagent finishes and `FORKED` comes straight back to the main line |
17:T9fe0,:Tc022,<p>想知道這些東西能不能像俄羅斯娃娃那樣一層包一層，就實驗了一下。Claude Code 自己能設定的是 skill、agent、tool、hook 四種，兩兩配起來十六種，一種一種跑。</p>
<ul>
<li><code>allowed-tools</code> 只允許 Read，skill 裡面 trigger Bash，Bash 即便不在 <code>allowed-tools</code> 還是可以跑</li>
<li>觸發帶 <code>hooks:</code> 的 skill 後，還在同一個 session 的話，hook 不會隨著 skill 結束消失</li>
<li><code>settings.json</code> 裡 hook 的事件名多打一個 e 這種低級 typo 變成 <code>PreToolUsee</code>，不會報錯也不會觸發。加 <code>--debug</code> 或 <code>--include-hook-events</code> 想檢查也沒有錯誤訊息，只有本來該出現的 hook 事件不見了</li>
</ul>
<p>環境：</p>
<ul>
<li>CLI 2.1.257，每一次都直接叫 <code>~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.257</code>，不走 <code>claude</code> symlink（它會自己更新）</li>
<li>Agent SDK 固定在 0.3.257</li>
<li>每個實驗都跑在 <code>-p</code>（<code>--print</code>）底下：給一句 prompt，跑完把結果印出來就結束，不開互動介面，也不跳任何對話框</li>
</ul>
<h2>model 跟 engine</h2>
<p><code>model</code> 是 Opus、Fable 那種跑在 API 那頭的語言模型。要叫 tool 的時候，它回覆裡會多一塊 <code>tool_use</code>：</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"tool_use"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"name"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Bash"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"input"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: {</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"git status"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>這段 JSON 是 model 寫出來的文字，<code>git status</code> 到這裡還沒跑。</p>
<p><code>engine</code> 是本機執行的那支 <code>claude</code> binary。它把工具清單交給 model，收到 <code>tool_use</code> 就去執行，執行前後還會去看 <code>settings.json</code> 裡有沒有 hook 要跑。</p>
<p>engine 每另外開一段 context 去做事，那段就叫 subagent。主線自己也算一段。每段 context 有自己的工具清單，主線一份，每個 subagent 各一份。</p>
<p>下面四種元件裡，skill 跟 agent 是磁碟上的 <code>.md</code> 檔，hook 寫在 <code>settings.json</code> 或 frontmatter，tool 沒有檔案。檔案本身不會做事，是 model 跟 engine 讀了以後才有行為。</p>
<h2>四個元件</h2>
<h3>tool</h3>
<p>tool 就是 model 能呼叫的函式，一個名字加一份參數 schema。</p>
<p>清單上有 <code>Bash</code>，沒有 <code>git status</code>。要 model 跑 <code>git status</code>，它發出來的是一次 <code>Bash</code> 呼叫，<code>git status</code> 是傳給 <code>Bash</code> 的參數。一個東西要成為 tool，得先登記進這個 session 的工具清單，沒登記 model 就看不到，也沒辦法呼叫。</p>
<p>清單上的 tool 本身不是 process。<code>Bash</code> 是一個名字加上參數格式，被呼叫的時候那行指令才交給 shell 去跑。</p>
<p>內建 tool 的名字是一個詞，像 <code>Read</code>、<code>Write</code>、<code>Edit</code>、<code>Bash</code>。</p>
<p>MCP server 給的格式如下：</p>
<ul>
<li><code>mcp__&#x3C;server>__&#x3C;tool></code></li>
<li><code>mcp__claude_ai_Jira__getJiraIssue</code></li>
</ul>
<p>大寫的 <code>Agent</code> 跟 <code>Skill</code> 也是 tool，跟 <code>Bash</code>、<code>Read</code> 排在同一份清單裡；小寫的 agent 跟 skill 是磁碟上的 <code>.md</code> 檔案，寫的是這個 agent 扮演誰、這份 skill 要做哪些步驟。開一個 subagent 就是 model 呼叫 <code>Agent</code>，跑一份 skill 就是呼叫 <code>Skill</code>。<code>SKILL.md</code> 自己不會執行，model 呼叫 <code>Skill</code> 之後才載入。</p>
<h3>skill</h3>
<p>skill 就是一份 <code>SKILL.md</code>，路徑是 <code>.claude/skills/&#x3C;名字>/SKILL.md</code>。放在專案目錄底下，只有那個專案有；放在 <code>~/.claude/skills/</code> 底下，每個專案都有。</p>
<p>檔案開頭兩行 <code>---</code> 中間夾的那塊叫 frontmatter，YAML 格式，設定都寫在那裡。第二行 <code>---</code> 底下是寫給 model 看的步驟。</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: hooktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then report in one line exactly what happened.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>model 看 <code>description</code> 決定什麼時候用它，內文是載入之後照著跑的程序。<code>SKILL.md</code> 就是一份文字，不會自己執行。</p>
<h3>agent</h3>
<p>agent 定義開出來的 subagent 是一段不帶主線對話紀錄的 context，接任務、自己做完、回結論給主線，中間過程不會進主線。CLI 跟 SDK 放定義的地方不一樣：</p>
<ul>
<li>CLI 讀 <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code></li>
<li>SDK 沒有檔案這一層。跑一個 session 的入口是 <code>query()</code>，同樣的內容當 <code>agents</code> 選項傳給它，欄位跟檔案裡一樣</li>
</ul>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">name: probe</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">description: Test agent for preloaded skills and tool limits.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">skills: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#DBEDFF;--shiki-dark-text-decoration:underline;--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-light-text-decoration:underline">secretskill</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">]</span></span>
